beats.text: Science never proved bumblebees cannot fly.
beats.note: The sums behind the story assumed a rigid, smooth wing, according to Snopes.

beats.name: Antoine Magnan
beats.role: Wrote in Le Vol des Insectes that applying air resistance laws made insect flight impossible. The sums were by his assistant.

beats.text: It treated a bee like a jumbo jet.
beats.note: Jumbo jets have fixed wings. The calculation only showed that bees with smooth, rigid wings cannot glide.

beats.context: How often a bumblebee beats its wings on average, according to Science News.

beats.note: Stroke angles change, and air flows over the wing in a way that creates lift. Snopes credits Torkel Weis-Fogh at Cambridge in the 1970s.

beats.text: Nobody agrees who did the sums.
beats.note: Some accounts name students of Ludwig Prandtl, others Swiss gas dynamicist Jacob Ackeret. The 1934 book is the earliest known reference.

beats.text: The bee was fine. The model was wrong.
